text: I’ll model the oil as the closed internal cavity: a cylinder of radius 23 mm and height 10 mm, minus the spinner annulus (15–22 mm radius, 8 mm high). This produces one connected oil region comprising the bore, radial clearance, and both 1 mm end gaps. Its boundary naturally splits into the ring bore wall, all spinner-wetted faces, and separate top/bottom cavity end faces. I’ll use a coarse snappyHexMesh first, after exporting all four conformal patch STLs in one call. First I’m checking the installed CAD API needed to construct and inspect that fluid solid.

The dimensions are converted once from millimetres to metres. I’m now creating the fluid cavity directly and measuring its volume, bounds, validity, and boundary-face geometry before assigning patches.

The solid is valid and single-region, with exactly seven boundary faces: three ring-side faces (wall and two ends) plus four spinner faces. The computed volume matches the analytic subtraction. I’ll now inspect a cutaway rendering so the bore, 1 mm radial clearance, and end gaps are visible rather than hidden by the closed cavity surface.

The cutaway confirms the intended topology. I’ll now classify faces by their intrinsic surface type, area, and plane elevation (not by bounding-box position), verify the requested 1 mm gaps and ring/spinner dimensions numerically, then export the four conformal patch STLs together. The “ring end” patches are the cavity-closing circular faces at the ring end planes; although the request calls them annular, the oil-filled spinner bore makes each fluid boundary face a full disk.

The face classification and every requested dimension checked correctly, but the export call used an unsupported keyword and therefore this cell will not be part of the reproducible build. I’m checking the installed helper’s exact signature before repeating that step.
I’ll repeat the semantic face assignment, measurements, and conformal export using the helper’s actual `out_dir` argument.

The four STLs were exported before meshing, and their welded union is closed with consistent winding. For the first mesh I’ll use a 1 mm Cartesian background grid and 0.5 mm surface refinement, giving roughly two refined cells across each specified 1 mm clearance while remaining coarse enough for quick inspection. The keep-point is in the central bore at the origin.
The coarse meshing dictionaries are ready. I’ll generate the background mesh first and verify its scale and cell count before cutting it to the oil region.

The background mesh is exactly 1 mm and 27,648 cells over the intended metre-scale domain. I’ll now run snappyHexMesh in-place to retain only the connected oil cavity and snap/refine its four named STL patches.
snappyHexMesh requires the standard empty `fvSchemes` and `fvSolution` dictionaries even though no solver will be run. I’ll add only those mesh-utility prerequisites, then retry.
The utility dictionaries are now present; I’ll rerun the coarse surface-conforming mesh.
The coarse oil mesh has 45,488 cells, with no mesher quality violations. I’ll now run the binding bare `checkMesh` and inspect topology, bounds, patch count, and quality.

`checkMesh` passes: one connected region, exactly four patches, 45,488 cells, maximum non-orthogonality 43.7°, maximum skewness 1.06, and mesh volume within 0.61% of the exact CAD volume. I’ll export the mesh geometry to VTK and render a cutaway to confirm that cells occupy the bore, radial clearance, and both end gaps.
The VTK export confirms the four named boundary datasets. I’ll now make the final cutaway mesh inspection image with cell edges visible and the patches overlaid in distinct colors.

The boundary overlay shows the correct patches, but the oblique cut still hides much of the internal connectivity behind the top end face. I’ll make a diametral \(x\)-\(z\) section, which directly exposes the bore, both radial clearances, and both axial gaps.

The diametral mesh section confirms a single connected oil region: the central bore connects through the 1 mm top and bottom gaps to both 1 mm radial clearances. The 30 mm outer radius belongs to the solid ring and therefore does not appear in the internal oil mesh; I am predicting a possible coverage advisory on that point and waiving it explicitly. No solver or boundary-condition fields were created.
